The eRA Product Manager within Notre Dame Research serves as the strategic owner of the University’s electronic Research Administration (eRA) ecosystem. This position is responsible for the vision, roadmap, governance, and lifecycle management of the administrative systems that support the University’s research enterprise.

The eRA Product Manager partners closely with Notre Dame Research Administration and Compliance, Campus IT, and external software vendors to ensure research administration and compliance platforms align with institutional priorities, federal compliance requirements, and the evolving needs of faculty and research staff.

In this role, the eRA Product Manager acts as a high-level consultant to University leadership, translating strategic research objectives into scalable technology solutions that improve operational efficiency, data integrity, compliance readiness, and proposal competitiveness.

Most immediately, the successful candidate in collaboration with the Associate Vice President of Research and the Director of Research Effectiveness and Analytics will play a defining leadership role in steering the University through a major eRA implementation, shaping the future of Notre Dame’s research infrastructure from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities Define, manage, and execute the product roadmap for the University’s electronic Research Administration systems, prioritizing enhancements and feature releases that streamline workflows and reduce administrative burden.

Serve as the primary liaison between Notre Dame Research Administration and Compliance, Campus IT, and third-party software vendors to advocate for institutional needs and influence product development.

Lead system governance and integration strategy for research administration platforms, ensuring effective data exchange between eRA systems, HRIS, ERP, and other enterprise applications. Oversee research data governance practices to establish consistent standards, improve data quality, and support reliable institutional reporting and analytics.

Configure and maintain system validations and workflows to support evolving federal regulations and sponsor requirements, including NSF, NIH, USDA, and other compliance standards. Collaborate with leadership and stakeholders to identify opportunities for process improvement, automation, and enhanced reporting capabilities.

Develop and maintain system documentation, business processes, and training materials to support successful adoption of system enhancements and transitions. Lead “train-the-trainer” initiatives and support change management efforts across the research community.

Monitor system performance, user feedback, and emerging industry trends to inform continuous improvement efforts. Support reporting and data visualization activities to translate research administration data into actionable insights for leadership decision-making.

Support audit readiness activities by ensuring accurate system configurations, data integrity, and compliance documentation. Participate in vendor user groups, professional organizations, and research administration communities to stay informed on best practices and emerging technologies.

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Research Administration, or a related field. 7+ years of experience in research administration, enterprise systems management, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in a leadership, Product Owner, Product Manager, or similar strategic systems role.

Experience supporting enterprise-level software implementations, preferably within research administration, ERP, or higher education environments. Expert understanding of the research grant lifecycle, including pre-award, post-award, and compliance functions.

Strong understanding of enterprise systems architecture, integrations, and data governance principles. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence stakeholders without direct supervisory authority. Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex data and identify operational trends.

Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences, including faculty and senior leadership. Ability to balance strategic planning with operational execution in a dynamic environment. Strong organizational and project management skills with attention to detail and compliance requirements.

Preferred qualifications Experience working within higher education research administration environments. Familiarity with eRA systems, ERP platforms, and SaaS-to-on-premises data integrations. Experience with reporting and visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI.

Knowledge of federal research compliance regulations and sponsored program administration. Please include a cover letter and resume to be considered for this role. Salary up to $113,500, commensurate with experience. Applications due by July 27 2026.

The University of Notre Dame seeks to attract, develop, and retain the highest quality faculty, staff and administration. The University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin, sex, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or age in employment.

Moreover, Notre Dame prohibits discrimination against veterans or disabled qualified individuals, and complies with 41 CFR 60-741.5(a) and 41 CFR 60-300.5(a). We strongly encourage applications from candidates attracted to a university with a Catholic identity.

The University of Notre Dame is more than a workplace; it is a vibrant, mission-driven community where every employee is valued and supported. Rooted in a tradition of excellence and inspired by our Catholic character, Notre Dame is committed to fostering an environment of care that nurtures the whole person—mind, body, and spirit.

Here, you will find a deep sense of belonging, a culture that prioritizes well-being, and the opportunity to grow your career while being a force for good in the world.

Whether contributing to world-class research, shaping the student experience, or supporting the University’s mission in other ways, you will be part of a dedicated team working to make a meaningful impact on campus and beyond. At Notre Dame, your work matters, and so do you! Originally posted on Himalayas

Job Description: We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning.

We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.

About the Role: The Product Manager, Applied Research Intelligence helps build Wiley ’s AI platform for life-sciences research and development — products that help scientists and R&D teams turn the world’s scientific literature and data into faster, better-evidenced decisions.

Working across the platform, you will partner with product, design, engineering, and data science to move features and improvements from idea to launch, and to keep what we build grounded in how researchers actually work.

You will contribute to product discovery with researchers and R&D users, help shape requirements and priorities, and track how your work performs once it ships. You’ll collaborate closely with senior product managers and the wider team across several workstreams, bringing the perspective of the life-sciences user to everyday product decisions.

This is a hands-on role with room to grow as the team and platform mature. Qualifications Product management experience (typically 5+ years) on B2B / enterprise software — ideally data, analytics, AI/ML, or platform products — contributing to products from discovery through launch.

Experience working in, or closely alongside, research and development in pharmaceutical or life-sciences organizations, with a good understanding of how scientists and research teams work. Ability to turn customer and market insight into clear requirements and measurable outcomes.

Comfort with technical concepts — data, APIs, and AI/LLM-driven workflows — and the ability to collaborate effectively with engineering and data science. Sound prioritization and judgment in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment, drawing on both qualitative and quantitative evidence.

Strong communication and collaboration skills across internal product, design, engineering, and commercial teams as well as external integration partners. Experience contributing to a product or product line that scaled to $50M+ in revenue, from build through launch. Preferred Qualifications An advanced degree (PhD or MS) in a life-sciences field.

Familiarity with scientific informatics tooling (ELN/LIMS, Benchling-class tools), knowledge graphs, or systematic-review and evidence-synthesis workflows. We power infinite possibilities. For more than 200 years, we've transformed knowledge into discoveries that shape the world.

Today, our global team of innovators, creators, and experts is driving what's next in science, education, and publishing—creating impact that reaches everywhere. We're not just observers of progress. We're the ones accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing learning, and sparking innovation that redefines entire fields and improves lives.

Here, your talent matters. Your ideas have room to grow. And your work creates breakthroughs that can change everything. Wiley is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer.

We evaluate all qualified applicants and treat all qualified applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or based on any individual's status in any group or class protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

Wiley is also committed to providing reasonable accommodation to applicants and employees with disabilities. Applicants who require accommodation to participate in the job application process may contact tasupport@wiley.com for assistance. We are proud that our workplace promotes continual learning and internal mobility.

Our values support courageous teammates, needle movers, and learning champions all while striving to support the health and well-being of all employees.

We offer meeting-free Friday afternoons allowing more time for heads down work and professional development, and through a robust body of employee programing we facilitate a wide range of opportunities to foster community, learn, and grow.

We are committed to fair, transparent pay, and we strive to provide competitive compensation in addition to a comprehensive benefits package.

Newsweek Recognizes Sedgwick as America’s Greatest Workplaces National Top Companies Certified as a Great Place to Work® Fortune Best Workplaces in Financial Services & Insurance Product Manager PRIMARY PURPOSE : The Product Manager represents the “voice of the client” by maintaining and prioritizing the product backlog that maximizes business value.

This position translates client needs into clear, actionable requirements. The Product Manager will solicit stakeholder input and feedback to inform product decisions and partners closely with the development team to balance functional outcomes with technical feasibility, manage dependencies, and support predictable delivery.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES Set product vision & roadmap Performs external and internal discovery to identify client needs, market opportunities, and business priorities, incorporating technical constraints, platform standards, and architectural considerations into product direction.

Collaborates with Operations, Sales, and Product leadership to ensure strategic alignment, secure sign‑off on key business decisions, and balance functional and technical tradeoffs.

Works with the Product Director to adjust scope, sequencing, and roadmap decisions, ensuring product functionality aligns with both business outcomes and technical feasibility. Defines product outcomes (OKRs), represents the “voice of the client,” and communicates roadmap progress, risks, and dependencies to stakeholders.

Oversee, coordinate & support development work Estimates effort required to complete requests and allocates capacity accordingly. Partner with Product Management and stakeholders to define business and functional requirements and gather necessary inputs. Defines user stories, acceptance criteria and prioritizes backlog to meet sprint goals.

Ensures product strategy, requirements, and priorities are well understood and effectively communicated to development teams, including through intake processes. Understands and helps coordinate intra‑team and external dependencies as applicable.

Collects, tracks, and reports KPI data to support Product Group OKRs and monitor performance metrics such as efficiency and quality. Represent the development team in work related to core delivery, non‑functional requirements, and technical initiatives (e.g., maintenance, support, and technical debt).

Participates in sprint ceremonies and evaluation meetings (e.g., planning, reviews, retrospectives). Contributes to or author IT and product documentation as needed. Tactical Maintains a holistic understanding of business processes and internal system configurations impacting the product and evaluates technical implications of proposed changes.

Assesses business process changes and system impacts to ensure features can be implemented effectively and sustainably. Serves as a primary contact for stakeholders, ensuring clear communication of requirements, risks, assumptions, and delivery decisions.

Provides product expertise, consultation, and support for release readiness, lifecycle management, and continuous improvement activities. ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS and RESPONSIBILITIES Performs other duties as assigned. Travel as required. QUALIFICATIONS Education & Licensing Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university preferred.

Licenses as needed. Experience Eight (8) years’ experience in product strategy, product management or requirements intake role. Experience with agile development is strongly preferred.

Skills & Knowledge knowledge of agile methodologies and tools and experience writing and managing user stories Cross‑functional collaboration, with the ability to build productive relationships with technical and non‑technical partners business and technology acumen, including understanding customer needs, technical concepts, and business strategy Effective communication skills, encompassing clear verbal, written, and presentation communication with diverse stakeholders Analytical and problem‑solving skills, with the ability to interpret data, assess tradeoffs, and inform decisions Organizational and time management skills, enabling prioritization of work, management of competing demands, and reliable delivery Leadership and influence skills, including people management, negotiation Professional execution and accountability, including producing quality written outputs, working effectively in team environments, and meeting or exceeding performance expectations WORK ENVIRONMENT When applicable and appropriate, consideration will be given to reasonable accommodations.

Join the Tilt team At Tilt , we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential.

With millions of customers worldwide , we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.

The Opportunity: Product Manager, Cash We're hiring a Product Manager for our cash products, the fast, high-volume liquidity products at the center of the business. You'll own meaningful surfaces of products used by millions, with the room and expectation to run big pieces yourself. This is a builder's seat on a highly analytical team.

You'll live in the data, work comfortably with analysis, design and read experiments, and move fast on a product where small changes compound across huge volume. We want someone self-directed enough to take an ambiguous problem, frame it, and drive it to a shipped result without a lot of hand-holding.

The people who thrive here set their own direction and don't wait to be told what to work on. Analytical horsepower is the baseline. We also want you to bring, and keep building, a real user point of view.

You'll have strong analytical partners around you, and the growth edge in this role is pairing that rigor with sharper instincts for the user experience. How You'll Make an Impact Meaningful surfaces of the cash products, from problem framing through experiment design, launch, and readout.

A steady cadence of experiments: you define the hypotheses, get the instrumentation right, and interpret results with an eye on timing and release mechanics. The trade-offs between business outcomes and user experience on a high-volume product where both matter.

Clear, direct communication of what you're doing and why, to a demanding, fast-moving set of stakeholders. Coordination with Compliance, Legal, Operations, Credit, Design, and Support on product changes, including regulatory reviews, support escalation workflows, and operational readiness.

What the First 90 Days Look Like By day 30: A working command of the product, the data, and the funnel. You know how the surfaces you own perform, where the friction is, and where the biggest experiment opportunities sit. By day 60: Sharp hypotheses on your top opportunities, with the first experiments designed, instrumented, and in build.

By day 90: Experiments live and reading out, with a prioritized backlog and a clear point of view on what to double down on next. Why You're a Great Fit Strong analytical foundation. You're fluent in data, experienced with dashboards and SQL, and you understand A/B testing, experiment timing, and release mechanics in depth. Self-direction.

You take a loosely defined problem and drive it forward on your own initiative. People who need a fully scoped brief to get moving struggle here. A builder's background. Nice to have if you’re a former engineer who moved into product and like to stay close to how things actually get built and measured. Strong communication.

You're clear, concise, and direct, and you can make your reasoning legible to a sharp audience. Drive and velocity. You move quickly and take real ownership of outcomes. Growing user instincts. You care about the user experience, not just the metric, and you want to sharpen that muscle. We'll support that growth.

Comfort operating in a regulated environment. You'll work closely with Legal, Compliance, Design, Credit and Support, seeking partnerships as part of the product process to deliver stronger outcomes. Consumer product experience is a plus. Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past.

If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you. What you'll get at Tilt Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity. Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.

Visibility is yours : You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly. Paid global onsites : Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures.

(We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.) Impact is recognized : Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines. The Tilt Way We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally.

We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible.

When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures. You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve. Compensation Range: $153K - $180K Originally posted on Himalayas

As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal.

The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.
What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

Du möchtest nicht einfach ein bestehendes Produkt weiterentwickeln, sondern eine neue technische Fähigkeit für unsere gesamte IT aufbauen? Dann könnte diese Rolle genau das Richtige für dich sein.
Mit deiner Leidenschaft für Softwareentwicklung, Automatisierung und CI/CD gestaltest du als technisch versierter Product Owner des System Teams unsere technischen Grundlagen, Plattformen und Standards rund um Software-Entwicklung und modernen IT Betrieb. In einer ersten Phase liegt dein Fokus auf drei zentralen Themen:

In einem nächsten Schritt entwickelst du das System Team gezielt weiter zu einem zentralen Enabler für weitere Teile des Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC):

* Du kannst eine klare Produkte-Vision erarbeiten und technische Themen strukturieren, priorisieren und in eine umsetzbare Roadmap übersetzen.
* Du agierst sicher in einem Umfeld mit verschiedenen Stakeholdern und schaffst es, gemeinsame Ziele und verbindliche Leitplanken zu etablieren und wirksam in einer Organisation zu verankern.

As we expand our scalable, affordable PACE model to meet the growing and complex needs of aging populations, our mission‑driven care teams continue to help participants live well on their own terms.

Role Scope
Habitat Health is hiring its first Data Product Manager to report to the VP of Product. We are looking for a generalist, hands-on, highly technical individual contributor who will own the roadmap for Habitat's data products and infrastructure, setting direction and priorities across the data function. You will own data products end-to-end across the two major Habitat Health pillars that the data team supports:
Platform & Integrations , including Engineering / IT / Product / Technical & AI vendors
Dashboards & Reporting , across growth, clinical, financial, and administrative data sets
In this role you will serve as the key bridge between our Product and Data functions, working closely with C-Suite and VP level stakeholders to align on the right product strategy, then rolling up your sleeves and collaborating with our development team to build data products that align with business needs. To succeed as a Data PM, you will need to balance Habitat’s high level business objectives against end user needs and development constraints.
In a given week you'll move across all of the modes below: figuring out what's actually worth building (Discovery), writing specs precise enough for developers to build from without back-and-forth (Specs), running the Jira backlog and sprint process (Delivery), keeping development unblocked (Execution management), mocking up and shipping dashboards (Design, QC, UAT), and triaging the daily stream of ad hoc requests from a diverse set of data customers (Triage).

s.h: Core Responsibilities & Expectations for the Role
s.t:
Discovery : define the business problem before the build (e.g. is automating LOPMR for CMS audits the right priority this quarter?).
Build and ship : own the full delivery cycle – specs, Jira/sprint process, dashboard design and sign-off, UAT, and rollout.
Hands-on data work : use SQL and Git to independently query, validate, and review code, not just manage a backlog.
Triage : distinguish quick fixes from roadmap work across a steady stream of ad hoc requests.
AI fluency : use AI tools (e.g. Claude) to accelerate the work and model that fluency for the team.
Range : move across all Platform & Integrations, Clinical & Operational Services, Regulatory and Enterprise Reporting, helping shape how data product works at Habitat.

3 to 5+ years of experience in product management, data/BI, or a closely related field, with a track record of shipping data products, dashboards, or reporting tools end-to-end (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
Solid understanding of healthcare data ontologies, systems, and information technology
Proficiency in SQL sufficient to independently query, validate, and troubleshoot data.
Demonstrated ability to write clear technical specs (metric definitions, cohort logic, source-to-target mapping ,etc.)
Experience partnering directly with business stakeholders and end users – e.g., operations, compliance, or clinical leadership – to gather requirements, design solutions, and lead user acceptance testing.
Familiarity with a modern data development stack (e.g., Jira, Git, Power BI, and cloud data platforms such as Databricks or Azure) sufficient to spec, review, and troubleshoot alongside engineering.
Comfort and enthusiasm using AI tools to enhance productivity in requirements writing, documentation, analysis, and workflow automation.
Aligns with our purpose and our values, and is excited about living those out in daily practice
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with comfort navigating ambiguity, adapting quickly, and contributing to continuous improvement
Strong learning and growth mindset, including seeking feedback, engaging in healthy debate and using data and curiosity to inform decisions.
Acts with integrity and ownership, considering the broader organizational impact, doing the right thing, and following through to deliver results.

Working knowledge of Agile/Scrum practices, including backlog grooming, sprint planning, and Jira (or similar tools).
Experience in PACE, VBC, or another regulated, compliance-driven environment, including deep working knowledge of healthcare data ontologies (e.g., CPT, ICD-10, NDC).
Experience with Epic (Clarity, Caboodle, Chronicles), medical/pharmacy claims data, or FHIR/HL7-based integrations.

To make this possible, we create, curate, acquire and champion visionary films, bringing them to audiences all over the world. We have a team of brilliant, dedicated and passionate people to help bring our mission to life. From London to New York, Istanbul to Paris, and Berlin to Mexico - we work together to realize MUBI’s vision.
That’s where you come in! Join our global team and help us make great cinema accessible to everyone, everywhere.

This is a senior, hands-on product role for someone who wants to own a meaningful slice of the MUBI product end-to-end, and is at their best when the problem is still ambiguous.
You’ll own the Audience & Platform Expansion domain - a critical product surface for our next phase of growth. In this role, you will be responsible for building the scalable foundation to drive global subscriber acquisition and pioneer our tiered premium offerings.

You’ll own its strategy, its roadmap and its delivery, from a high-level business goal all the way to a shipped, measured feature. The hardest product problems at MUBI cross team and time-zone boundaries, and break down without someone holding the whole picture; this role exists to be that person for one of these domains.
Reporting to our Senior Product Director, this is a senior, individual contributor role. You'll lead through clarity and influence rather than headcount - aligning engineering, design and data scientists around a vision they actually believe in, and mentoring/coaching other, more junior PMs as you go. We care about craft, in the films we champion and in the products we build, so the bar is product excellence and real user impact, not shipping for its own sake.
We work hybrid-remote where we require 3 office days in Soho, London (if you're in commutable distance from London). Our core days are Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday, with the flexibility to use our offices on the remaining two days if you wish.
Where you'll have impact
You'll own a product surface that leadership relies on, translating ambiguous, evolving priorities into a roadmap teams can execute against - and giving the business a crisp, honest read on what's working, what isn't, and what needs a decision. As you build credibility through delivery, you'll set the standard for how product strategy is articulated and defended at MUBI. Concretely, you'll:
Translate business goals into clear, actionable product roadmaps, and own the sub-strategy for a specific MUBI area (e.g. onboarding, content/catalogue discovery, monetization, or viewer experience).
Guide technical products through the entire lifecycle - from conception, through development, into launch - and iterate after.
Partner directly with Engineering, UX/UI Design, Data Science, Marketing, Business Development and Legal to define product requirements and resolve trade-offs.
Establish the KPIs and OKRs for your area, and use data-backed insight to iterate quickly and demonstrate measurable impact.
Pitch roadmaps to senior leadership to guide resource allocation, and align engineering, design and analytics teams without relying on direct hierarchy.
Write narrative strategy memos and present complex visions clearly - to senior leadership and engineering teams alike.
Mentor other team members and raise the bar for product thinking around you.

You've spent significant time shipping complex technical products end to end, and you're happiest owning a problem from the messy, ambiguous start rather than picking up a tidy backlog. You bring structure where there is none - a clear strategy, sharp prioritisation, honest measurement - without becoming a source of process for its own sake.
You're technically fluent enough to hold your own with strong engineers: you can translate an ML model, a streaming architecture or a latency constraint into a business trade-off a stakeholder can act on, and tell a real architectural limit from a convenient one.
You're an excellent communicator who can flex between an engineer and an executive in the same hour, equally comfortable writing a strategy memo and defending it in a leadership review.
You lead through influence - aligning people across functions, regions and time zones around work they want to do.

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Design, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years in product management or a closely related technical role, with at least 3–5 years focused on shipping complex technical products from 0 to 1.
Strong business judgment and strategic thinking - able to see the big picture and make connections across teams and issues.
Technical acumen: the ability to translate highly technical engineering constraints (machine learning models, streaming architectures, latency) into clear business trade-offs for non-technical stakeholders.
Deep domain fluency in identity and access management, subscription management, billing and monetization, and data processing - with the ability to debate architectural and technical trade-offs.
A proven ability to lead cross-functional teams through influence rather than direct authority.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, including narrative strategy writing for senior audiences.
Strong problem-solving, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Experience with AI tools, and AI prototyping
A deep alignment with MUBI's culture and values: craftsmanship, product excellence, a bias toward high-impact work, and genuine respect for the user.

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions.
The team’s execution has been exceptional and we are scaling at a remarkable pace. Our early team brings experience from J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, PayPal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium and others, and we are backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NFX and other top-tier investors.

We are looking for a Product Operations for Latin America to own how new currencies and corridors actually get to market across the region. Every currency we launch unlocks new corridors for our institutional clients and drives trading volume and revenue directly.

Your mandate is to make that expansion happen on the ground: sourcing and onboarding liquidity providers, standing up settlement rails with banking partners, clearing jurisdiction-specific regulatory requirements, and holding every launch to the reliability bar our clients expect.
You will run the regional launch pipeline with real independence. You will own pricing inputs, sequencing and the go-live decision. You report to the Product Leader of Global Payments & Currencies, who sets strategic prioritisation for which currencies matter most based on payout corridor relevance. You own the how and the when.
If you have shipped cross-border payment products, worked with banking or card network infrastructure, or built API-driven financial products across jurisdictions, this role will feel familiar. The difference is that you will be doing it at the frontier of stablecoin-settled FX infrastructure, where the rails are new and the playbook is yours to write.

Own corridor launch, end to end. You own every currency in your regional pipeline from Alpha through General Availability. You track liquidity partner onboarding, settlement rail readiness, regulatory clearance, operational setup and pricing. You run readiness reviews, maintain the launch checklist, and make the go/no-go call.
Operationalise our licences. Holding a licence and being able to use it are two different things. You work with Product Management, Legal and Regulatory, Compliance, Finance and Engineering to turn each licence, registration and partner permission into permitted product scope, documented operating procedures and live client flows.

You keep what we are authorised to do and what we actually run in market in step, and you make sure new capability reaches clients as soon as the licence allows rather than months later.
Work directly with LPs and banking partners. You are the product voice in liquidity provider onboarding and banking partner discussions. You understand what it takes to stand up a new currency pair technically, what banking partners need in order to enable settlement, and how to translate partner constraints into product decisions.
Navigate multi-market regulatory complexity. Every currency carries jurisdiction-specific requirements. You work with Legal and Regulatory to establish what is needed, translate it into product and engineering decisions, and ensure no currency launches without clearance.
Prioritise engineering effort. You work with engineers to deliver against the roadmap. You write specs, set sprint priorities, and partner with your EM so capacity lands on the highest-impact currencies.
Drive post-launch adoption. A currency is not done at launch. You track whether clients are actually trading new corridors, partner with GTM to drive activation, find the friction, and feed what you learn back into prioritisation.
Build the regional launch playbook. You turn each launch into a repeatable, documented process covering every dependency, gate criterion and handoff, so the tenth currency is faster than the first.

Must-haves
8+ years in product management, product operations or programme management. You have owned a complex, multi-dependency delivery process in a B2B or infrastructure product.
Cross-border payments or financial infrastructure context. You have worked on payments, FX, card networks or digital asset products.
Multi-market experience. You have shipped products across multiple countries or regulatory jurisdictions.
Comfort operating between product, legal and compliance. You can read a regulatory requirement, work out what it means for a product flow, and drive it to a decision without waiting to be told.
Operational rigour. You maintain systems that track complex, multi-dependency work. You build the checklist, follow up on the open item, and catch the gap before it becomes a blocker.
Based in Brazil, in São Paulo or remote, and fluent in Portuguese and English.
What helps you stand out
LatAm corridor knowledge. Experience with Brazilian and wider LatAm payment rails, regulatory environments or banking partner ecosystems. Spanish is a plus alongside Portuguese.
Licensing and regulatory delivery. You have helped operationalise a licence, registration or scheme membership, not just tracked one.
Card network or payment scheme background. Time at a card network, payment scheme or large-scale processor with multi-market product launches.
Stablecoin or digital asset rails. Familiarity with stablecoin settlement, on and off-ramp infrastructure, or crypto payment products.

Equity in a rapidly growing company
The chance to work in a fast-paced startup at the forefront of fintech innovation
Real impact on global financial infrastructure

Über die Position
Gestalte mit uns die digitale Infrastruktur des europäischen Gartenbaus
Connected Growers entwickelt June: Die Plattform, über die Erzeuger, Käufer und Vermarkter effizient zusammenarbeiten. Wir ersetzen fragmentierte Prozesse durch moderne Software und schaffen eine gemeinsame digitale Infrastruktur für eine ganze Branche.
Dafür suchen wir einen Product Manager (m/w/d) für unseren Bereich Grower Experience, der gemeinsam mit Engineering und Design unsere Anwendung für Gartenbaubetriebe weiterentwickelt.

Als Product Manager Grower Experience (m/w/d) verantwortest du die Produktentwicklung unserer Anwendung für Gärtner*innen. Du berichtest direkt an unseren CPO.
Deine Nutzer sind Gartenbaubetriebe, deren Bedürfnisse Du durch enge Zusammenarbeit mit diesen und weiteren Experten der Branche kennenlernst. Du entwickelst daraus technische Lösungen und Standards für die Branche.
Du definierst relevante KPIs für deinen Produktbereich und misst den Erfolg deiner Arbeit konsequent an ihnen.
Anforderungen
Was du mitbringst
Mindestens 4–5 Jahre Erfahrung im Produktmanagement von B2B-Softwareprodukten.
Erfahrung im eigenständigen Führen von User Interviews, Bereitschaft zu unregelmäßigen Vor-Ort-Besuchen bei Gärtner*innen. (Führerschein erforderlich)
Kenntnisse gängiger Tracking- und Analytics-Tools.
Exzellente schriftliche Kommunikation (Roadmaps, PRDs).
AI-Erfahrung am Puls der Zeit: Du bist bei neuen Entwicklungen up-to-date und findest wege, wie du AI für Deine Arbeit und eingebettet im Softwareteam effizient nutzen kannst.
Fließend Deutsch, sehr gutes Englisch.
Das wäre ein Plus
Erfahrung mit Prozessen aus der Warenwirtschaft oder aus dem Handel.
Ein Software-Background kombiniert mit Product-Management-Erfahrung.
Aufgabenbereich
Was du bei uns bewegst
Du verantwortest die Produktstrategie und -roadmap für den Bereich Grower Experience.
Du sprichst wöchentlich eigenständig mit unseren Gärtner*innen, baust Beziehungen zu ihnen auf und triffst die Betriebe in unregelmäßigen Abständen auch vor Ort.
Du arbeitest eng mit Design und Engineering zusammen, leitest gemeinsam mit Design User Interviews und übersetzt die daraus gewonnenen Erkenntnisse in konkrete Produktentscheidungen, während Du das Team fachlich durch den gesamten Produktentwicklungsprozess führst.
Du verstehst und artikulierst den Business Value deiner Produktentscheidungen, u. a. über KPI-Frameworks, und nutzt Tracking- und Analytics-Daten, um Annahmen zu validieren und Produktentscheidungen datenbasiert zu treffen.
Du kommunizierst Roadmaps, PRDs und Produktentscheidungen klar und überzeugend – schriftlich wie mündlich.
Du nutzt AI selbstverständlich in deinem Alltag – für Prototyping, eigene Datenanalysen und einen effizienten, AI-gestützten Produktentwicklungsprozess gemeinsam mit deinem Engineering-Team.
Deine Arbeit hat direkten Einfluss auf unser Produkt, unsere Kunden und den Erfolg von June.

Unsere Produktteams verantworten ihre Bereiche vollständig: von der Produktstrategie über User Research und Priorisierung bis hin zum Release und den kommerziellen KPIs ihres Bereichs.
Gemeinsam mit Design und Engineering übernehmt ihr Verantwortung für den Erfolg eures Produktbereichs und arbeitet kontinuierlich daran, ihn zu verbessern.
Wir sprechen regelmäßig mit unseren Kunden, besuchen sie vor Ort und testen unsere Lösungen gemeinsam mit ihnen. Wir glauben, dass gute Produktentscheidungen nur entstehen, wenn man die Probleme der Nutzer wirklich versteht.
Wir arbeiten pragmatisch, treffen Entscheidungen früh und passen sie an, wenn neue Erkenntnisse entstehen. Wir haben starke Meinungen, halten aber nicht dogmatisch an ihnen fest. Verantwortung endet bei uns nicht mit dem Release.

Was dich erwartet
Die Möglichkeit, Produktverantwortung für einen der zentralen Bereiche von June zu übernehmen.
Die Chance, den europäischen Gartenbau grundlegend zu verändern
Ein erfahrenes Design, Product und Engineering-Team an deiner Seite.
Großer Gestaltungsspielraum für Produktstrategie und Roadmap.
Viel Verantwortung und kurze Entscheidungswege.
Modernes, AI-gestütztes Arbeiten im gesamten Produktentwicklungsprozess.
Die Möglichkeit, unsere Produktkultur aktiv mitzugestalten.
Hybrides Arbeiten in unserem Büro in Köln sowie regelmäßige Besuche bei den Gärtner*innen vor Ort.

As the developer of the world's leading software AMOS, Swiss-AS manages successfully maintenance, engineering and logistics requirements of modern airlines.

To strengthen our position at the forefront of this global market, we are looking for dedicated employees who would like to work in a fascinating international environment with more than 200 customers worldwide.**
To strengthen our Product Management team in Basel, we are looking for an experienced Product Owner with a strong background in aviation maintenance and production planning.

As Product Owner, you will shape the future of **Production Planning for Aircraft Maintenance**. You will combine your aviation expertise with your product management skills to turn complex operational challenges into valuable software solutions.
You will work closely with customers, aviation experts, Product Management, and software development teams to define the right solutions and bring them successfully to market.
**Tasks**
* Own the **product vision, roadmap, and backlog** for Production Planning.
* Understand customer and industry needs and translate them into clear product requirements.
* Prioritize development activities based on customer value, business goals, and strategic priorities.
* Collaborate closely with software development teams during solution design and delivery.
* Act as the link between customers, aviation experts, and software development.
* Validate product outcomes through customer feedback, product performance, and continuous improvement.
* Stay up to date with aviation regulations, industry standards, and emerging technologies.
* Build relationships with industry experts and contribute to the evolution of industry standards through working groups and conferences.
**Skills**
* Experience as a **Product Owner, Business Analyst, or in a similar software product role**.
* Strong knowledge of **aviation maintenance and production planning**.
* Experience with **MRO software or aviation-related systems** is highly desirable.
* Understanding of Agile product development principles.
* Ability to translate complex business needs into clear software requirements.
* Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
* A degree in aviation engineering, computer science, or a related discipline is an advantage.

* Working in an open and cooperative environment with a motivated and friendly team
* Flexible working hours (flex time model)
* Hybrid work model
* Flight and travel discount
* Excellent working conditions in pleasant surroundings
* Good professional and personal development opportunities
* Highly appealing pension fund scheme/retirement savings plan
* An international work environment with people from around the globe
**Workplace & Culture**
This is the environment where your meaningful work impacts our customers, our communities and everyone who experiences AMOS. You develop technical skills, increase your knowledge about aviation and new technologies, meet different cultures, and always be yourself.

Your work significantly impacts people's lives, technically and as human beings, and contributes to the formation of our future. In addition, you can be part of a fantastic multicultural and international team with a family spirit. We love to travel, laugh, work, be creative, play sports, and, last but not least, do our best work together.

Dans le cadre d-un programme de transformation digitale et industrielle, nous recherchons un(e) IT Product Owner - Customer Service pour accompagner l-évolution des processus et des systèmes d-information d-un environnement industriel exigeant.
Intégré(e) à une équipe de Transformation Digitale, vous interviendrez sur le périmètre Customer Service, notamment autour des activités liées aux réparations et à la gestion du stock.
Vous serez le relais opérationnel entre les équipes métier et IT. Votre objectif : comprendre et challenger les besoins métier, proposer des solutions systèmes pragmatiques, les traduire en spécifications fonctionnelles et piloter leur réalisation jusqu-à leur mise en production et leur fonctionnement en Run.
Vous évoluerez dans un environnement applicatif comprenant notamment SAP CS, PLM, BI/Data ainsi que différentes applications métier.

* Recueillir, analyser et challenger les besoins métier afin d-identifier les problématiques et opportunités d-amélioration.
* Identifier et proposer, avec les équipes IT, des solutions fonctionnelles et techniques adaptées.
* Traduire les besoins métier en spécifications fonctionnelles claires.
* Gérer et prioriser le backlog en collaboration avec les différentes parties prenantes.
* Piloter les projets et évolutions de bout en bout, de la définition du besoin jusqu-à la mise en production.
* Coordonner les équipes IT, métiers, experts techniques, intégrateurs et partenaires externes.
* Organiser les phases de tests et de validation métier, puis accompagner les déploiements et mises en production.
* Assurer le suivi post-déploiement et du Run, en veillant à la robustesse, la maintenabilité et la pérennité des solutions.
* Contribuer à l-amélioration continue des processus métier et à l-adoption des solutions par les utilisateurs.
## Ce que nous recherchons : ##
Vous disposez idéalement de 3 à 5 ans d-expérience en Product Ownership, gestion de projets IT, analyse fonctionnelle ou transformation digitale.
Vous combinez une vraie sensibilité IT avec de solides compétences en gestion de projet. Vous comprenez les systèmes d-information et savez faire le lien entre les enjeux métier et les équipes techniques, sans nécessairement être vous-même développeur.
Une expérience dans un environnement Customer Service, industriel/Manufacturing, Supply Chain ou opérations constitue un réel atout. Une connaissance de SAP CS, PLM, BI/Data ou d-applications métier serait également appréciée.
Vous êtes autonome, pragmatique, structuré(e) et orienté(e) solutions. Vous savez faire avancer les sujets, prioriser, prendre des décisions et collaborer efficacement avec des interlocuteurs métier, techniques et externes.

Own the AI Receptionist product end-to-end

Revenue Growth Management (RGM) is one of The Coca-Cola Company's most important commercial capabilities, and not simply a pricing discipline. Coca-Cola positions RGM alongside brand building, innovation, and integrated execution as a core capability for topline growth, and our growth strategy names it a key commercial capability for determining where to play and how to win.
RGM connects consumer demand to the economics of the system. It determines what we sell, in which packages, at what price points, through which channels and customers, and with what promotional investment, all in service of balanced growth across transactions, volume, and price/mix.

Done well, it finds incremental revenue pools and converts them into commercial action, improves the economics of every price, pack, assortment, and promotion decision, builds the affordability and premiumization ladders that bring more consumers into the portfolio, and gives Coca-Cola and its bottlers a common fact base for growing customer revenue and profit rather than simply negotiating price.
We are now reimagining RGM for the agentic AI era, and we are building it ourselves.

Our Global RGM Product is evolving from a suite of analytical solutions into an intelligent decision platform where AI agents interact directly with enterprise data, invoke advanced analytics and optimization models, run and compare scenarios, and hand commercial teams a recommendation with the reasoning attached.

Work that once took an analyst a week (pulling the data, running the model, writing the story, defending the number) is being compressed into a conversation.
Few companies are attempting this at this scale, and fewer are still against decisions this consequential: real pricing, promotion, and portfolio moves, made across markets and bottlers. The work sits at the frontier of the CPG industry, spanning agent orchestration, retrieval over enterprise data, and the evaluation of non-deterministic and deterministic systems, and none of it is a research exercise. What we build ships to commercial teams who use it to make decisions the same week.
This is an opportunity to build, not just design, the next generation of commercial decision intelligence at Coca-Cola, and to establish the operating model for agentic RGM at global scale. The patterns set here will shape how one of the world's largest commercial systems makes its most important decisions. If you want your work in front of real users, at real scale, from the first release, this is that role.

As Product Manager, RGM, you will own the what and the why of the Global RGM product: which problems it solves, for whom, in what order, and how success is measured. You will work within a persistent, cross-functional product team alongside Data Science, Engineering, UX, Architecture, and RGM experts. Engineering owns how the product is built; you own everything that determines whether it is worth building.
Product direction starts in market. You will spend time with RGM teams at operating units and bottlers to understand how pricing, promotion, and portfolio decisions are actually made, where current ways of working break down, and which problems are worth solving next. You will convert that discovery into direction: clear problem statements, a prioritized roadmap, and requirements that tell the team not just what to build, but why it matters commercially.
Day to day, this is a product ownership seat. You will write user stories and acceptance criteria, prioritize the backlog against commercial value, define what 'good' looks like for each release, and sign off that what shipped does what the business needed.

It demands genuine fluency in what the product produces (elasticities, uplift against baseline, share math) and in the commercial world those recommendations land in.

You will stay engaged across the full product lifecycle, from discovery and pilot design through launch, adoption measurement, and continuous improvement - because adoption is the truest test of whether you defined the right product.
The role is global across a commercial system that spans more than 200 countries and territories, roughly 200 bottling partners, and 30 million retail customer outlets - few products anywhere offer a larger canvas. It is also a first seat: the product discipline you establish here becomes the pattern for how the Global RGM Product scales to every market.

s.h: What You Will Do for Us
s.t:
Own the product roadmap for the Global RGM suite: define the problems worth solving, sequence capabilities by commercial value, and present the roadmap and the value delivered to OU leadership and bottler executives.
Run continuous discovery with users: sit with RGM managers and walk a run end to end (which price moves to take, which to skip, and why) to understand where the product creates value and where it falls short.
Translate discovery into direction: turn user pain into written requirements with clear problem statements, examples, and acceptance criteria, and retest with the same users once a fix ships.
Write user stories the engineering team can build against, and represent the voice of OUs and bottlers in prioritization and roadmap decisions with the Global RGM Product Owner.
Own and prioritize the product backlog against commercial value, with the judgment to say no, sequence competing requests, and defend a prioritization call to senior stakeholders.
Define the success measures for each release, participate in backlog refinement and sprint reviews with the pod, and give business sign-off that shipped functionality does what the market actually needed.
Guard the product's credibility by catching recommendations that would not survive scrutiny in front of a bottler, before the bottler sees them.
Embed the closed-loop RGM workflow in the product (insight generation and opportunity sizing, strategy setting, guardrail definition, in-market execution, and post-implementation evaluation) so markets operate a consistent, repeatable process.
Design for governance: make RGM rules of engagement (price floors and ceilings, discount depth and promotion frequency, and price-gap and price-index thresholds) capabilities the product enforces rather than policies applied around it.
Support pilot design and test-and-learn discipline with market teams: hypothesis framing, control groups, and incrementality measurement.
Partner with the AI engineer on insight quality, rating generated insights and flagging output the underlying data does not support.
Partner with the UX designer on launch communication, naming, and demo material so each release lands with the business.
Build the business case for significant capability requests: size the commercial opportunity, weigh it against effort and alternatives, and make the call on what is worth building.
Lead each release to adoption: launch planning, capability building, and short playbooks (how to read an elasticity, when to trust a recommendation), with the goal of users opening the product without you.
